chronology_correction.issue: Some r147-r152 artifact/checkpoint filenames and created_at values were assigned from an estimated elapsed wall-clock rather than an authoritative clock and can be later than their actual repository commit time.
chronology_correction.resolution: Treat checkpoint_revision plus repository commit chronology as authoritative, not the nominal filename timestamp for r147-r151 or result-artifact created_at fields. This r152 checkpoint uses a fresh current-time read. No research semantics depend on those nominal timestamps.

milestone.name: provider-verified signed-commit premise succeeds for preexisting external repository evidence
milestone.negative: Own role-local connector-created commit remained unsigned and is rejected by the same origin rule.
milestone.revision: PCBE-like proof chains can admit a new premise origin, PROVIDER_VERIFIED_COMMIT, for a file frozen inside an already-signed exact GitHub commit. Chat does not independently verify raw cryptography; it trusts GitHub's provider-reported verified=true, reason=valid and exact immutable commit/tree/file identities. This is read-only reuse of preexisting verification evidence, not fresh signing or arbitrary signature verification.

provider_verified_commit_file.hosted_compute_boundary: No on-demand verification job launched; preexisting repository verification metadata was read under the repository-evidence exception. Trust is explicitly GitHub-provider trust, not independent crypto.

fresh_authenticated_manifest_authorship.reason: current connector writes are unsigned and expose no signing operation

negative_evidence: Mutable branch references are insufficient for this premise; exact signed commit SHA is mandatory.
Provider verified status is not equivalent to Chat independently verifying the signature.
Already-signed evidence does not solve fresh signing.
A signed commit authenticates the commit/tree under provider trust; semantic meaning of a file still requires explicit parsing/proof rules.

frontier.action: Formalize a generic premise lattice and composition rule: OWN_REPO_IDENTITY, PROVIDER_VERIFIED_COMMIT_FILE, DECLARED_CONFIG and DERIVED accepted under distinct scopes; EXTERNAL_OBSERVATION and RAW_SIGNATURE remain rejected. Test a mixed proof that combines one provider-verified public file identity with one own-repo identity and declared config.

Test whether a signed annotated Git tag exposes provider verification suitable for immutable release identity; compare exact-tag object versus signed commit and reject mutable release names that are not frozen to exact verified objects.
Extend content-semantic claims only for small readable text explicitly parsed under a bounded grammar; never infer binary semantics from signed identity alone.

exact_next_action: Build one mixed-origin finite certificate: require RELEASE_MODE=1, own r145 payload blob identity exact, and external sigstore/cosign README identity 263924df... at provider-verified commit 58aae9.... Derive MIXED_OK=1 only if all three accepted-origin checks pass. Negative controls must independently flip own identity, external commit verification flag, exact-ref file identity and config.
